rounds.text: Market Creators Ltd is displaying clear signs of an active operational turnaround that sentiment has yet to price in, evidenced by a quarterly operating margin of -1% in June 2026 compared to -8% in the year-ago quarter, marking a solid 7 percentage point improvement [E29]. This momentum is corroborated by impressive screening signals highlighting a net profit surge of 83% year-over-year alongside 20% year-over-year sales growth [E50, E52]. Crucially, results score a remarkable 98 out of 100 on an accelerating basis, warning us not to dismiss a genuine turnaround story on stale market sentiment [E55]. Furthermore, the business is demonstrating financial discipline by actively trimming its borrowings to ₹ 5.95 Cr in March 2026 down from ₹ 6.07 Cr the prior year [E36], all while maintaining strong historical share price compounding of 31% over five years [E21]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months have suffered steep sales and profit contractions alongside negative operating and free cash flows [E16, E19, E33, E34].

Market Creators Ltd carries fundamental risks and an inflated valuation that the underlying business performance fails to support. Compounded sales growth has stagnated at 0% over 3 years and a paltry 1% over 5 and 10 years [E13, E14, E15], cratering further in the trailing twelve months with a massive -64% drop [E16]. Profitability metrics are deeply concerning, highlighted by a TTM compounded profit growth of -120% [E19] and a meager 5.6% ROCE combined with a -1.5% ROE in filed statements [E11, E12], alongside flagging issues for low interest coverage [E43], high borrowing costs [E47], and poor 3-year ROE [E45]. Furthermore, cash generation is severely distressed as operating and free cash flows plunged to Rs -9.84 Cr and Rs -9.92 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E33, E34], exacerbated by ballooning debtor days from 59.9 to 80.5 [E46] and working capital days skyrocketing from 280 to 653 [E48]. Speculative enthusiasm has heavily outpaced fundamental reality, evidenced by a price-led divergence where 5-year share price growth of 31% massively outstrips a -1% profit growth [E18, E21, E40], an expensive EV/EBITDA of 30.63x versus a 13.42x sector benchmark [E10], and zero dividend yield [E3]. conceded: [E52]

The bear points to stagnant multi-year sales growth [E13, E14, E15, E16], but ignores the powerful turnaround captured in the results score of 98 out of 100 where sales jumped 20% year-on-year alongside an 83% surge in net profit [E50, E52, E55]. While cash flow and working capital metrics are under pressure [E33, E34, E48], the business is actively de-leveraging with borrowings ticking down to Rs 5.95 Cr from Rs 6.07 Cr [E36], and quarterly operating margins have staged a sharp recovery of 7 percentage points to -1% in June 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E29]. The bear's critique of historical return metrics [E11, E12] overlooks that the company's ROA of 13.64% and ROE of 13.93% substantially outperform sector benchmarks of 1.93% and 4.92% respectively [E7, E8]. Furthermore, stale sentiment completely misses that quarterly results are accelerating rapidly while prices remain cautious [E55]. conceded: [E3, E10, E43, E46, E47]

The bull points to recent sales and net profit surges [E50, E52] and a high results score [E55], but these fail to contextualize a severe multi-year structural decline where compounded sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years sits at 1%, 1%, and 0% respectively, culminating in a disastrous -64% TTM contraction [E13, E14, E15, E16]. While the bull highlights a 7 percentage point quarterly margin improvement to -1% [E29], operating margins remain fundamentally in negative territory and volatile, with the yearly trend explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E30]. The bull’s reliance on select return metrics [E7, E8] ignores the company's own filed statements showing a negative TTM ROE of -1.5% [E12], a median 3-year ROE of 0% [E26], and a miserable 10-year median ROE of just 1% [E24]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes balance sheet stress, yet the company registered a catastrophic negative operating cash flow of Rs -9.84 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -9.92 Cr for Mar 2026 [E33, E34], alongside surging working capital days expanding from 280 to 653 days [E48]. Conceded: [E29, E50, E52, E55].
